n: Manama, City of Trade, Multiculturalism and Religious Coexistence
na: المنامة، مدينة التجارة والتعددية الثقافية والتعايش الديني
s: Historic port town of souqs and many faiths · UNESCO Tentative List 2018
dr: UNESCO Tentative List, submitted 20 July 2018 (ref. 6354, criteria ii, iii)
el: More than 120 places of worship of four religions
te: The harbour town of many faiths
se: Old Manama grew from a busy harbour into a town of more than 450 shops and over 120 places of worship for four religions
sa: نمت المنامة القديمة من ميناء مزدحم إلى مدينة تضم أكثر من 450 متجرًا وما يزيد على 120 دار عبادة لأربعة أديان
desc: Manama lies on the northern coast of Bahrain’s main island; Bahrain’s harbour moved here in the 19th century from Qal’at al-Bahrain. By 1904 the town had more than 450 shops in its souqs, including Souq al-Ajam and Souq al-Yahud, and the region’s first municipal government was set up here in 1919. More than 120 places of worship of four religions stand in the town, among them the Sri Krishna Temple, Bahrain’s largest Hindu temple, a synagogue, mosques and three main churches. The National Heritage Register includes 31 houses in Manama.
sig: A historic Gulf trading town where communities of different faiths have lived side by side.
refs: UNESCO World Heritage Centre. Manama, City of Trade, Multiculturalism and Religious Coexistence. Tentative List ref. 6354, submitted 20/07/2018. https://whc.unesco.org/fr/listesindicatives/6354
conf: Coordinates are the UNESCO Tentative List point (N26 13 59, E50 34 44) converted to decimals. t0 is a broad estimate for the 19th-century move of the harbour (present ≈ 2000). Arabic title is a translation of the English UNESCO title; an official Arabic title was not found. Historic urban property; fits the archaeological layer loosely.

s: Bapco’s 1930s garden-city oil town · UNESCO Tentative List 2019
dr: UNESCO Tentative List, submitted 4 March 2019 (ref. 6397, criteria ii, iv)
te: The garden town built for oil
se: From 1934 the Bahrain Petroleum Company built Awali, a garden town of about 400 buildings for its oil workers
sa: منذ عام 1934 بنت شركة نفط البحرين مدينة عوالي، وهي مدينة حدائق تضم نحو 400 مبنى لعمّال النفط
desc: Awali, in Bahrain’s Southern Governorate, has been built since 1934 by the Bahrain Petroleum Company (Bapco) as a settlement of about 400 buildings, mostly from the 1930s and 1940s with upgrades in the 1950s. Its layout follows the European garden city and garden suburb movements, with houses around a central green and offices in a central location. Housing ranges from bunkhouses for male workers to family houses and small villas, most with private gardens. The UNESCO entry notes the region’s first central sewage system and the world’s first centralized air-conditioning system for an entire settlement.
sig: An early planned oil town that records the start of the oil industry in the Arabian Peninsula.
disc: Garden-city layout around a central green
refs: UNESCO World Heritage Centre. Awali oil settlement. Tentative List ref. 6397, submitted 04/03/2019. https://whc.unesco.org/fr/listesindicatives/6397
conf: Coordinates are the UNESCO Tentative List point (N26 5 15.57, E50 32 53.55) converted to decimals. t0 from 1934 (present ≈ 2000). Arabic name not taken from an official Arabic text. Distinct from the app’s first-oil-well entry about 5 km to the south.

s: Offshore pearl oyster bed · UNESCO World Heritage 2012 and marine protected area
dr: UNESCO World Heritage 2012 (component 1364rev-002 of Pearling, Testimony of an Island Economy); marine protected area, SCE Resolution No. 3 of 2017
el: 4,854.77 ha inscribed area; about 57 km from mainland Bahrain
te: The oyster bed with the most pearls
se: Far out at sea, this oyster bed gave a recent survey its highest share of oysters carrying pearls
sa: بعيدًا في عرض البحر، سجّل هذا الهير في مسح حديث أعلى نسبة من المحار الحامل للآلئ
desc: Hayr Bu ‘Amamah is one of the three offshore oyster beds of the World Heritage property Pearling, Testimony of an Island Economy, inscribed in 2012, with an inscribed area of 4,854.77 ha about 57 km from mainland Bahrain. A hayr is a flat rocky seabed deeper than 10 m dominated by pearl oyster beds. A 2025 survey at 15.9–16.9 m found up to 47 oysters per m², with Pinctada radiata making up 81.3% of the bivalve community at one site, and the study’s highest pearl incidence (14.3%) at the other. It was declared a marine protected area by Supreme Council for Environment Resolution No. 3 of 2017.
sig: One of the three living oyster beds that carry the marine part of Bahrain’s pearling World Heritage property.

s: Offshore pearl oyster bed · UNESCO World Heritage 2012 and marine protected area
dr: UNESCO World Heritage 2012 (component 1364rev-001 of Pearling, Testimony of an Island Economy); marine protected area, SCE Resolution No. 3 of 2017
el: 5,659.13 ha inscribed area; about 58 km from mainland Bahrain
te: Home of the biggest pearl oysters
se: On this deep offshore oyster bed, divers measured the largest pearl oysters found in a recent survey
sa: في هذا الهير العميق في عرض البحر قاس الغواصون أكبر محار لؤلؤ وُجد في مسح حديث
desc: Hayr Bul Thamah is one of the three offshore oyster beds of the World Heritage property Pearling, Testimony of an Island Economy, inscribed in 2012, with an inscribed area of 5,659.13 ha about 58 km from mainland Bahrain. It was first declared a marine protected area in 2007 and is now protected under Supreme Council for Environment Resolution No. 3 of 2017. A 2025 survey at 16.2–20.6 m depth found coarse sand over bedrock with up to 30 oysters per m² and the largest oysters in the study, up to 8.2 cm.
sig: One of the three living oyster beds that carry the marine part of Bahrain’s pearling World Heritage property.
disc: Largest oysters in the 2025 survey, up to 8.2 cm

s: Offshore pearl oyster bed · UNESCO World Heritage 2012 and marine protected area
dr: UNESCO World Heritage 2012 (component 1364rev-003 of Pearling, Testimony of an Island Economy); marine protected area, SCE Resolution No. 3 of 2017
el: 24,569.6 ha inscribed area; about 30 km from mainland Bahrain
te: The biggest oyster bed in the Arabian Gulf
se: The largest of Bahrain’s heritage oyster beds is crowded with young oysters, corals and sponges
sa: أكبر مغاصات اللؤلؤ التراثية في البحرين يعجّ بالمحار الصغير والمرجان والإسفنج
desc: Hayr Shtayyah is the largest of the three offshore oyster beds of the World Heritage property Pearling, Testimony of an Island Economy, inscribed in 2012, with an inscribed area of 24,569.6 ha about 30 km from mainland Bahrain. A 2025 survey at 10.9–12.1 m depth found 54–67 oysters per m², the highest proportions of young oysters (spat) in the study at 41.9% and 55%, and hard coral cover of 22.6% at one site. It had the highest biodiversity of the northern sites, with hard and soft corals, sponges and anemones. It was declared a marine protected area by Supreme Council for Environment Resolution No. 3 of 2017.
sig: The largest of the three living oyster beds that carry the marine part of Bahrain’s pearling World Heritage property.
